**A tissue box cover's tissue hole now has a smooth, rounded edge - printed without supports.** The web version has it too: <https://rickusinggithub.github.io/vaseinator/>.

### Download & run (Windows)
1. Download **Vaseinator.exe** below and run it. It is one file: nothing to unzip or install. SHA256SUMS.txt holds its checksum.
2. The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info → Run anyway**.

No Python needed. To run from source on any OS, see the README. Or just use it in your browser: <https://rickusinggithub.github.io/vaseinator/>.

### Changed in 1.15.2
- **The tissue hole's edge is rounded**, both sides, for the tissues to slide over instead of catching on a sharp edge. The cover's top thickens round the hole to 2.4 mm, and the edge is rounded 1.2 mm each side.
  - The cover prints upside down, its top on the bed, so on that side the edge is a **chamfillet**: a chamfer from the bed leaning 43°, running into the round where it is that steep. Nothing needs supports.
  - The opening is still the size you set, where it is narrowest.
  - The holes in the wall - patterns, a mask's eyes and mouth, strap slots - can already have rounded edges: Advanced ▸ Holes and openings ▸ **Rounded edges**.

Vaseinator is free. If it has made you something you like, you can [buy me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/rickapps).
